quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and wait until the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed carefully. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: To merge into a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check behind you and watch the vehicle ahead. Make sure no vehicles are in your way in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Slow down, check traffic, and gradually turn back when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way street to a one-way street, enter the first lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending. Get ready for merging traffic.

questions.question: What problem can bad suspension cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and provides a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Cars passing you.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: You must yield to oncoming vehicles. You can only turn when it is safe and you will not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What happens when driving on gravel or dirt roads?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less traction, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less traction, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less traction on gravel and dirt than on pavement. Slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid.

questions.question: You are behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use the whole lane.
Honk to make the motorcycle move so you can pass.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane. Never share the same lane. Moving back too soon can force the rider to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent collisions.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Wait for time to pass.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your system quickly but leaves slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol content. The only way to lower it is to wait.

questions.question: When should a driver not pass another vehicle on a two-lane road?

options.text: On a hill.
In a curve.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass another vehicle when driving in a curve, on a hill, or in any no passing zone. You may only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm out?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, stop completely. Stay stopped until the stop arm is raised and the flashing lights turn off.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from a car's headlights coming toward you?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Look at the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. After looking briefly to the side, continue looking ahead to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: Your wheels have left the road pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the steering wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and apply the brakes gently. Slow down, check traffic, and find a safe place to merge back onto the road. Jerking the wheel back can cause you to lose control or hit other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign appears on one-way streets and roads where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to go the wrong way on an expressway ramp.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use turn signals?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when pulling up to a curb and when leaving it.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left side of the cab.
On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have very large blind spots. The driver cannot see your car behind them. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: The center of the road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken line is next to your lane, what does it mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When one yellow line is solid and one is broken, you can pass from the side next to the broken line.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic light colors from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: This sign alerts drivers that a traffic signal is ahead at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
You must turn right in this lane.
You can only turn right when the green arrow lights up.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs have a yellow or yellow-green background. They warn you about upcoming road conditions, such as curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?

options.text: To make drivers frustrated about traffic.
To slow down drivers.
To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and direct you safely through the area.

questions.question: When a school bus has red flashing lights, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students have left the bus.
The stop arm goes back in.
The stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights and a stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Stay stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm goes back in, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: If you see a single broken white line on a highway, you may:

options.text: Not cross the line to pass other cars.
Cross the line to pass and change lanes.
Cross the line to change lanes only if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road has many curves ahead.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
A side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance work ahead.

questions.question: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road as far as possible and stop.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road as far as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle with its siren and flashing lights. Move to the right edge and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the vehicle passes.

questions.question: You and the driver on your left both arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You do.
Whoever is signaling a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You do.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep scanning for possible hazards ahead and around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning for possible hazards ahead and around you.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for potential hazards. Do not just stare at the road right in front of you. Scan ahead and watch for vehicles around you.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go if it is safe.
Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop completely and wait until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot. You might miss them if you only glance quickly. Always watch for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross the center to pass other vehicles from your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the right lane will end ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge into another lane.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up to turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected green arrow is ending soon. You must be ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, what should you do?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use light braking.
Apply the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas pedal and let the car slow down. Use light braking only after the vehicle has slowed significantly.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn them.
Let them go first.
Swerve around them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them go first.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows the person is blind. Be careful and courteous. Let them safely cross before you drive forward.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your car.
Do not drive beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on both sides. Do not stay beside them for long because the driver may not see you.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, you should:

options.text: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to prevent them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use low gear before going downhill on slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. Stay farther back from other vehicles than normal. Avoid sudden stops. Pump your brakes only if your car does not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: Why do large trucks need extra space in front of them?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
To give the truck enough distance to stop.
So other drivers have room to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give the truck enough distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are heavy and need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when can you safely move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the car over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until both headlights of the passed vehicle are visible in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back to your original lane.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Let traffic only from your right pass.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must let traffic in the intersection pass first. You can continue without stopping if no traffic is coming. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It has no effect on driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right side of the road and stop. On one-way streets, move to whichever edge is nearest.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dark street, you should:

options.text: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beams to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep dashboard lights bright so others can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Drive slower and make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights show.

questions.question: The traffic light is green but traffic blocks the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partly enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
Drive in and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can get you a ticket.

questions.question: You are in the intersection when the green light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, keep going and exit the intersection as quickly as you safely can.

questions.question: How can you spot an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
They have many passengers in the car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for aggressive drivers who make sudden or unsafe lane changes. The safest thing to do is stay away from them and let them pass.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is a yield sign. Slow down and be ready to stop. Stop at the marked line if one exists.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Construction is ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone can pass if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no traffic coming from the other direction.

questions.question: When is the road most slippery?

options.text: After it has rained for several hours.
When rain just starts.
After it has rained for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just starts.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, dirt and oil on the road mix with water. This creates a slippery coating on the pavement.
